lead: Orlando's renters, short-term rentals, lightning and all-electric homes shape its fire damage. SootMend helps homes and businesses across the city recover from fire, smoke and soot.
risk: kitchen and electrical fires, lightning fires, and fires in apartments and vacation rentals
why: More than nine in ten Orlando homes heat with electricity, and most need heat only a few days a year. Cooking, dryers, electrical problems and lithium-ion batteries cause most fires. Central Florida also gets frequent summer lightning that can start attic fires.

About six in ten Orlando households rent, many in large apartment complexes, and the area has many vacation and short-term rentals. Pine flatwoods on the edges of the metro burn in dry springs; Orange County had FEMA fire assistance during the 2001 Orlando Complex Fire. Humid air speeds soot staining.
problems: Metro West, Conway and Lake Nona
tips: Clean dryer lint traps every load and vents yearly.
Charge e-bikes away from exits and never overnight.
Post fire exits and alarm info inside vacation rentals.
Run AC or dehumidifiers after a fire.
insurance: Many Floridians are insured through Citizens Property Insurance, and vacation rental owners need a policy that covers rental use.
areas: SootMend works across Orlando, including Downtown, College Park, Thornton Park, Baldwin Park, Dr. Phillips, Lake Nona, Conway and Metro West.

faq.q: Who pays for fire damage in an Orlando vacation rental?
faq.a: The owner's rental or landlord policy covers the building and owner's furnishings. Guests' belongings fall under their own insurance. A standard homeowners policy may not cover rental use.
